content:
Quick comments for now. I'll do a more detailed review once the points below have been addressed.

Goal
* Typo: instable => unstable

* level 2 add plates and tiles: I understand that you're planning a Level 2 version of the puzzle. Could you briefly explain what additional mechanics this introduces? An example test case would be helpful.

Input
* Typo: numbr => number

* Please change '" " separated' to 'space-separated'.

* Please remove "First is the brickName, second is the brickSize, next is the brickColor and finally the brickCount", and then list the fields individually like this:

• [[brickName]] (string): [description]
• [[brickSize]] (integer): [description]
• [[brickColor]] (string): [description]
• [[brickCount]] (integer): [description]

* For [[H]] and [[W]], please change "Line" to "Next line".

* Please change "[[N]] next" and "[[H]] next" to "Next [[N]]" and "Next [[H]]" respectively.

Constraints
* Please move the current constraint to the Output section, since it describes the required output order.

* Please write one constraint for each input variable.

Stub generator
* Please use the same variable names as those defined in the Input section.

Cases
* In Pacman (Test 5) and Pacman (Validator 5), one brick type has [[brickCount]] = 0. Is it necessary to cover this scenario?

* The following validator cases are identical to their corresponding test cases:
  • Black & white (Test 4) and Black & white (Validator 4)
  • Pacman (Test 5) and Pacman (Validator 5)
  Please revise the validators so that they cover the same scenario as the corresponding tests but with slightly different inputs and outputs.

* Please remove the trailing newlines from the input for:
  • Simple (Test 1)
  • Pacman (Validator 5)

* Please remove the trailing newlines from the output for:
  • Simple (Test 1)
  • Pyramid (Test 2)
  • Pyramid (Validator 2)
  • Battlements (Test 3)
  • Battlements (Validator 3)
  • Black & white (Test 4)
  • Black & white (Validator 4)

Thanks.

>All bricks are 1 large

What is 1 large? It is a bit confusing reading that at the beginning of the blurb.
Ok, depth is better I presume.

Thanks for comments.

It's my first contribution, so I test possibilities. :-)
I think I could work on new test cases, I haven't explored all the possibilities.

I wonder about the usage of LEGO word wich is a trademark ? Using LEGO makes problem easier to understand when I use vocabulary like brick, stud, plate, tile.

For level2, I imagine the wall described excatly like for level 1 but with the constrant to have flat upper. With the example given on level 1, you'll have to finish with 2 plates and 1 tile.

While it's fine to mention LEGO once at the beginning, and use LEGO terminology, players shouldn't be expected to know the vocabulary beforehand. The statement should define relevant terms and explain any properties that are relevant to the puzzle.

I don't understand how Test 1 can be completed with 2 plates and 1 tile in the proposed Level 2 version. Could you explain that to me?

Goal
* I'd recommend replacing the text *before the example* with something along the following lines:

#####

The goal is to build a wall using a given set of LEGO-style bricks.

<<Bricks>>

Each brick has:
• a name,
• a size,
• a color, and
• a limited quantity.

A brick of size [[brickSize]] occupies [[brickSize]] consecutive cells in a row. Bricks cannot be rotated. All bricks have depth 1.

You may be given more bricks than are required to build the wall.

<<The wall>>

The wall has depth 1.

The input describes the wall as a front view. Each non-space character represents a wall cell of a given color. A space represents a window and must remain empty.

Two bricks are <<connected>> if at least one cell of one brick rests directly on a cell occupied by the other brick.

A wall is <<stable>> if all placed bricks belong to a single connected component.

<<Building instructions>>

Your task is to output the sequence of brick placement instructions used to build the wall. Each instruction specifies:

• which brick to place, and
• the position of its leftmost cell (0-based).

Bricks are placed from bottom to top and from left to right. The row (vertical position) of each brick is therefore determined by the order of the instructions.

Only stable walls are valid solutions.

#####

* Please change "Example :" to "<<Example>>" (bold, no colon).

* Please format the example input using a monospace code block, i.e.
```
2
b1 1 W 6
(etc.)
WWW
```

* Please format the example output in the same way.

* Please change:
In previous example, using b1 bricks instead of b3 make the wall unstable.
to:
Using b1 bricks instead of a b3 brick on either the top or the bottom row makes the wall unstable.

* Please remove the remarks about Level 2. They aren't needed; I only asked about Level 2 to better understand your puzzle design plan.

Input
* Please change "[[N]] next" to "Next [[N]]".

* Please correct the typo: lenght => length.

* Please change "[[H]] next" to "Next [[H]]".

Constraints
* Please provide one constraint for each input variable.

Cases
* Battlements (Validator 3): Please remove the trailing newline from the output.

* Pacman (Test 5) and Pacman (Validator 5): One brick type has [[brickCount]] = 0. Is it necessary to cover this scenario?

* As mentioned last time, please revise the validators for Pairs 4 and 5 so that they cover the same scenario as the corresponding tests while using slightly different inputs and outputs.

I've reached the maximum comment length. Could you please address the points above first, and then we can continue with a further review?

Thanks.
